policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere מְשׁוּבוֹתֵיהֶם and ketiv משבותיהם are the same noun in plene and defective spelling; ASV 'their backslidings are increased' renders the plural noun with possessive suffix and cannot distinguish the orthography. The only note on the verse ('Or, deserts') is classed alternative_rendering, about the English word choice for the preceding forest/wilderness term, so it decides nothing here. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.

Qere אֶסְלַח and ketiv אסלוח are the same first-person imperfect of סלח, differing only in the plene waw; ASV 'How can I pardon thee?' renders that verb identically under either spelling. The verse note ('Or, according to another reading, made them swear') is classed alternative_rendering and attaches to the swearing clause, not to this lemma, so it does not select. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.

Qere יוֹרֶה and ketiv וירה both give the former rain, the ketiv adding a prefixed waw. ASV 'that giveth rain, both the former and the latter, in its season' pairs the two rains with 'both ... and', an English correlative that reads equally naturally over an asyndetic יורה ומלקוש or over a conjoined וירה ומלקוש; there is no ASV note mapped to this unit. Nothing in the English distinguishes the conjunction, so the base fallback (qere) carries the projection.
